label: County fertility equilibrium
summary: Whether the county's projected fertility equilibrium compares in the given way to a number.
details: The game warns that this check is very heavy and should only be used at your own risk. Works on a county (a title). Compare with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Faith fervor
summary: Whether the faith's fervor compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla compares it against plain numbers (for example `>= 60` or `< 75`) and against named script values such as `medium_fervor_value`.

label: Arrival date
summary: Whether the estimated date of arrival at the travel plan's final destination compares in the given way to a date.
details: Works on a travel plan. The value must be a valid date, for example `1100.1.1`. Supports `<`, `<=`, `=`, `>` and `>=` (not `!=`).

label: Days until arrival
summary: Whether the estimated number of days until the travel plan reaches its final destination compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a travel plan. The game's documentation calls the value an estimate. Supports `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` and `>=`.

label: Travel progress
summary: Whether the travel plan's progress towards its final destination, a value from 0.0 to 1.0, compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a travel plan. Progress is measured in time, counted from the departure date at the very start of the plan. For example `> 0.5` means more than half the time has passed.

label: Focus progress
summary: Whether the character's progress in their current focus compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation does not say what scale the progress uses, and vanilla gives no examples in the input.

label: Fort level
summary: Whether the province's fort level compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a province. Vanilla uses it both with exact values from 0 to 4 and with comparisons such as `> 0` and `>= 10`.

label: Adventure legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Adventure legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Adventure track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Pillage legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Pillage legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Pillage track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Coterie legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Coterie legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Coterie track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Urbanism legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Urbanism legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Urbanism track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Khvarenah legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Khvarenah legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Khvarenah track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Free building slots
summary: Whether the number of free building slots in the province compares in the given way to a number.
details: A building that is still under construction counts as using a slot. Works on a province. Vanilla mostly checks `> 0`, `0` or `>= 1`.

label: Free external domicile slots
summary: Whether the number of free external building slots of the domicile compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a domicile. The documented example is `scope:domicile = { free_external_domicile_building_slots < 1 }`. Vanilla mostly checks `>= 1` up to `>= 6`.

label: Free personal tenet slots
summary: Whether the number of personal tenets the character can still choose compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a character. It is always 0 for dead or non-playable characters. Vanilla mostly checks `> 0`.

label: Free tradition slots
summary: Whether the number of free tradition slots of the culture compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a culture. The documented example is `scope:culture = { free_tradition_slot > 1 }`. Vanilla uses it once, as `> 0`.

label: Game start date
summary: Whether the start date of the bookmark the game was launched from compares in the given way to a date.
details: The input lists no required target, so it needs no particular scope. Vanilla uses it to tell the bookmarks apart: exact dates such as `1066.9.15`, `867.1.1` and `1178.10.1`, or comparisons like `>= 1066.1.1`. Supports `<`, `<=`, `=`, `>` and `>=`.

label: In region
summary: Whether the province lies in the given geographical region.
details: Works on a province. Write the key of a region from the game's geographical regions, for example `world_europe` or `world_india`. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: GHW attackers' strength
summary: Whether the maximum military strength of the pledged attackers in the Great Holy War compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a Great Holy War. 'Maximum' means the strength if all levies were fully reinforced. Vanilla compares it with a named script value.

label: GHW defenders' strength
summary: Whether the maximum military strength of the pledged defenders in the Great Holy War compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a Great Holy War. 'Maximum' means the strength if all levies were fully reinforced.

label: GHW war chest gold
summary: Whether the amount of gold in the Great Holy War's war chest compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a Great Holy War.

label: GHW war chest piety
summary: Whether the amount of piety in the Great Holy War's war chest compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a Great Holy War.

label: GHW war chest prestige
summary: Whether the amount of prestige in the Great Holy War's war chest compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a Great Holy War.

label: Global list size
summary: Whether the number of entries in a global variable list compares in the given way to a number or script value.
details: The list is a global variable list, found by its name. The documented usage line is written for `variable_list_size` (with a `target` field), but vanilla uses this key with `name` and `value`, as in `{ name = laamps_tally value >= 1 }`.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The name of the global variable list.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the list's size.
fields.values: a comparison such as `>= 1` with a number or script value

label: Glory legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Glory legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Glory track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Gold
summary: Whether the character has the required amount of gold.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla mostly writes a comparison such as `> 0` or `>= 500`, or a named script value; it also uses `< 0`, so the amount can be negative. Vanilla also has a block form with `value` and `multiply` (for example `{ value = feudalize_holding_interaction_cost multiply = 4 }`). Going by the field names, it checks the value times the factor; the input does not document that form.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount to check against (block form).

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: A factor the value is multiplied by (block form).

label: Government allows
summary: Whether the character's government allows the named thing.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation does not list the possible names; the ones seen in vanilla are `merit`, `noble_families`, `state_faith` and `barter`.

label: Government disallows
summary: Whether the character's government forbids the named thing.
details: Works on a character. Going by its name it is the reverse of `government_allows`. The input shows no vanilla use, so which names are valid is not confirmed here.

label: Government has flag
summary: Whether the character's government has the given flag.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses it mostly to tell the kind of government apart, with flags like `government_is_nomadic`, `government_is_tribal`, `government_is_theocracy` and `government_is_feudal`.

label: Government has mechanic
summary: Whether the character's government has the given mechanic.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation lists these mechanics: feudal, mercenary, holy_order, clan, theocracy, administrative, landless_adventurer, herder, nomad, mandala. Vanilla uses `administrative` almost every time.

label: Government type has flag
summary: Whether the government type has the given flag.
details: Works on a government type itself, not on a character. Vanilla checks flags such as `government_is_theocracy`, `government_is_feudal` and `government_is_clan`. To check a character's government, use `government_has_flag` instead.

label: Project build progress
summary: Whether the great project's build progress, from 0 to 1, compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a great project. If the project is not being built, the value is 0. For example `> 0.5` means more than half is built.

label: Construction phase
summary: Whether the great project is in the given construction phase.
details: Works on a great project. The phases are `planned` (gathering funds), `in_progress` (building has started) and `completed`. The documented example writes `great_project_construction_phase`, without `_is`; vanilla uses the `_is` key shown here.

label: Days to completion
summary: Whether the number of days until the great project is built compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a great project. The estimate includes progress bonuses from the current province holder. If the project is not being built, the value is -1.

label: Project type
summary: Whether the great project is of the given type.
details: Works on a great project. Write the key of the project type from its definition, for example `great_wall`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The project type to check for.

label: Project type is important
summary: Whether the great project type is marked as important.
details: Works on a great project type, not on a project. The game uses the mark to drive its notifications. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Guile legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the Guile legacy track compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says 'perks in the lifestyle' and names no track. The Guile track is an inference from the key name, so treat it as likely, not confirmed.

label: Has access to MaA
summary: Whether the character has access to the given men-at-arms type.
details: Works on a character. Men-at-arms access gained through tributaries does not count. Write the key of a men-at-arms type, for example `horse_archers` or `kheshig`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The men-at-arms type to check for.

label: Accolade category
summary: Whether any of the accolade types has the given category flag.
details: Works on an accolade. The documented wording ('any of the Accolades types') does not say which types are meant. Vanilla uses categories such as `men_at_arms`, `ethical`, `aggressive`, `defensive` and `champion`.

label: Accolade parameter
summary: Whether any unlocked rank of the accolade has the given parameter flag.
details: Works on an accolade. Only ranks already unlocked count. Vanilla checks parameters such as `accolade_increase_control_bonus` and `acclaimed_knight_prestige_from_victory`.
